claim_as_stated: SPEED Act passed the House (Dec 18, 2025); current Senate status; key provisions (150-day limitations period; standing tied to substantive comments).
correct_statement: H.R. 4776 (SPEED Act, Rep. Westerman) passed the House 221-196 on Dec 18, 2025 (Roll Call 356); same day received in the Senate and referred to the Committee on Environment and Public Works. No later Senate action is recorded (latest action Dec 18, 2025); not enacted. As passed: claims generally barred unless filed within 150 days of publication of final agency action; where a comment period occurred, only parties that submitted a 'substantive and unique comment' may sue; remand is the sole remedy, with the action left in effect during a 180-day cure period; 'substantial deference' codified; effects limited to those with a 'reasonably close causal relationship' to the project.
source_title: H.R. 4776 timeline (congressional record data); SPEED Act Passes House (Law and the Environment blog)
source_publisher: The Lobby News (Congress.gov data mirror); Foley Hoag LLP
note: Status taken from a Congress.gov data mirror; re-check congress.gov immediately before publication. Separate Senate bill S. 3224 (statecraft) not checked. Describe as 'passed House; pending in Senate EPW', not as law.

claim_as_stated: NEPA s.112 sponsor-funded expedited reviews (180-day EA / 1-year EIS) - status and use.
correct_statement: NEPA section 112, added by the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (Pub. L. 119-21, signed Jul 4, 2025), lets a project sponsor pay a fee of 125% of the anticipated cost of preparing or supervising the document in exchange for deadlines of 180 days for an EA (from fee payment) and 1 year for an EIS (from the NOI). Sponsors submit a project description and a declaration on whether they will prepare the document under NEPA s.107(f) to CEQ, which must set the fee within 15 days. The provision is in force; CEQ maintains an intake page on nepa.gov.
source_title: Section 112 NEPA Project Sponsor Opt-In Fees; The One Big Beautiful Bill Act Offers Expedited NEPA Review for a Fee
source_publisher: Council on Environmental Quality (nepa.gov); O'Melveny & Myers
note: Use: no public count or list of projects using s.112 found (not-found for the 'use' half). The CEQ page does not state the 125% figure; it comes from the statute as summarized by counsel. The claim that s.112 does not speed ESA/NHPA reviews is a reasonable reading (the section covers only NEPA documents) but was not confirmed in a source this pass.

claim_as_stated: ESA 'harm' definition rescission - final? effective date; litigation.

claim_as_stated: OMB M-25-21 and M-25-22 (Apr 2025) on federal AI use and acquisition; M-26-04 (LLM procurement) and M-26-05 (secure software, rescinding M-22-18/M-23-16), Jan 2026.

correct_statement: M-25-21 ('Accelerating Federal Use of AI through Innovation, Governance, and Public Trust') and M-25-22 ('Driving Efficient Acquisition of Artificial Intelligence in Government') were issued Apr 3, 2025, replacing M-24-10 and M-24-18; M-25-22 applies to contracts from solicitations issued about 180 days after issuance (late Sep/Oct 1, 2025) and requires contracts to bar training publicly or commercially available AI on non-public agency data without explicit consent. claim_as_stated: California SB 253/261 status and first reporting dates (SB 253 first reports due ~Nov 10, 2026?); EU CSRD Omnibus I thresholds (>1,000 employees, >EUR 450m turnover).
correct_statement: California: OAL approved CARB's initial SB 253/SB 261 regulation on Oct 12, 2026 (effective immediately). SB 253 first reports (Scope 1 and 2) are due Nov 10, 2026 for U.S. entities with >$1 billion annual revenue doing business in California; Scope 3 reporting begins in 2027. SB 261 enforcement is enjoined by the Ninth Circuit pending appeal (since Nov 2025) and CARB says it will not enforce it while the injunction stands. EU: the Omnibus I Directive amending CSRD and CSDDD was published in the OJ on Feb 26, 2026 and entered into force Mar 18, 2026; CSRD scope is now EU undertakings/groups with >1,000 employees and >EUR 450m net turnover (non-EU groups: >EUR 450m EU turnover in each of the last two years plus an EU subsidiary/branch >EUR 200m); CSRD transposition by Mar 19, 2027. CSDDD now covers >5,000 employees and >EUR 1.5bn worldwide turnover (non-EU: EUR 1.5bn EU turnover), transposition by Jul 26, 2028, compliance from Jul 26, 2029.
source_title: California's Climate Disclosure Regulations Receive Final Approval Ahead of November Reporting Deadline; EU Sustainability Omnibus Published in the Official Journal

claim_as_stated: FAA Part 108 (BVLOS) rule status; American Security Drone Act / FCC Covered List effects on agency drones.
correct_statement: Part 108: FAA's NPRM 'Normalizing Unmanned Aircraft Systems Beyond Visual Line of Sight Operations' was published Aug 7, 2025 (FR Doc 2025-14992); comment period was reopened in Jan 2026; the final rule has been at White House (OIRA) review since Jul 10, 2026 and had not been published as of Oct 21, 2026, well past the Feb 1, 2026 deadline in EO 14307. ASDA (American Security Drone Act of 2023, enacted in the FY2024 NDAA): from Dec 22, 2025, covered UAS from foreign adversary-linked manufacturers (notably PRC) may not be procured, operated or maintained with federal funds; state DOTs implementing for FHWA-funded work cite OMB M-26-02. FCC: on Dec 22, 2025 the Public Safety and Homeland Security Bureau added all foreign-produced UAS and UAS critical components to the Covered List (FY2025 NDAA s.1709 national security determination received Dec 21, 2025), barring new equipment authorizations; previously authorized models may still be imported, sold and used, though an Oct 28, 2025 FCC order lets the FCC restrict previously authorized covered equipment later.
source_title: FAA Part 108 Delay: BVLOS Rule Stuck at OIRA (2026); DroneXL BVLOS news; FCC Adds All Foreign-Made Drones to Covered List; New Federal Restrictions on Foreign Drones (Effective Dec 22, 2025)
source_publisher: PickDrones; DroneXL; Holland & Knight; Missouri Department of Transportation
note: Part 108 status rests on trade press (no final rule found in Federal Register searches); re-check federalregister.gov before publication. Field-craft's 'still not published as of July 2026' should be updated to 'at OIRA since Jul 10, 2026; unpublished as of late Oct 2026'.
